articleTitle: Techno-Economic Analysis of the FTTH-GPON Sharing Infrastructure for Property Developers Using What-If Scenario Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Workshop on Fiber Optics in Access Networks (FOAN)
abstract: Fiber to the Home (FTTH) is often used to satisfy the increasing bandwidth and access speed requirements associated with the rapid growth of telecommunication technology. In this case, a few concerns such as continuous installations on poles, cables, underground grids, and the exclusive business model have been observed in the expansion of Internet Service Providers (ISPs) to some property areas. A multi-provider solution is available on Gigabit Passive Optical Network (GPON) technology through the integration of several ISPs into the FTTH sharing infrastructure. Therefore, this research aimed to provide a techno-economic analysis of FTTH-GPON sharing infrastructure developed and invested by property developers. The results showed that several ISPs could be integrated through the application of Virtual Local Area Network (VLAN) in FTTH-GPON sharing infrastructure. The investment of property developers was also projected to be profitable in the long run despite the significant initial CAPEX. Moreover, the 10-year projection for a property with low occupancy showed feasible revenue growth compared to not investing. This was confirmed by the NPV of 14,978 USD, the IRR was 12.21%, and the payback period was 7 years. The What-If Scenario Analysis also showed that the occupancy rate was the primary source of investment uncertainty. As a neutral operator, the property developers could set a minimum Average Revenue per User (ARPU) price regulation to ensure fair competition and prevent a “pricing war”.

articleTitle: Passive Optical Network Testing and Deployment at Telekom Slovenije
publicationTitle: 2024 International Workshop on Fiber Optics in Access Networks (FOAN)
abstract: Fixed access networks have evolved from legacy copper infrastructure to fibre. The deployment of fibre is crucial for the development of a gigabit society. The majority of networks currently in use are based on a point-to-multipoint topology. By deploying new Passive Optical Network (PON) technologies, providers can offer their customers a better service and provide a baseline for new applications that require high bandwidth and lower latency. For every new technology that is being deployed, there are some key milestones that need to be crossed. Two of the most important factors are standardisation and interoperability. Vendor locking is not a viable option in current deployments; vendors must cooperate to provide interoperability. Providers must also play an active role in this process, as their influence on vendors is significant. It is crucial that vendor proprietary solutions are not confirmed and deployed. The Broadband Forum introduced the BBF.247 ONU Certification program, based on the ONU Conformance Test Plan document TP-247. In conjunction with standardised test procedures, it is incumbent upon the provider to undertake real-case test scenarios with their own specific configuration. A significant aspect of the standardisation of the Gigabit Passive Optical Network (GPON) is the ONU Management and Control Interface (OMCI), which is the source of the majority of interoperability issues. Providers are constructing their optical distribution network for future use, with the objective of deploying all new PON technologies over the same network. In order to deploy new technology, it is necessary to either swap or upgrade existing active equipment. XGS-PON technology, which is a successor to GPON with a symmetrical speed of 10 Gbit/s, is being deployed using a comboPON solution. Concurrently, Wi-Fi 7 is being developed on residential gateways, which represents a significant driver for the extensive deployment of XGS-PON. The advent of 25 Gigabit Symmetric Passive Optical Network (25GS-PON) and 50-Gigabit-capable passive optical networks (50G-PON) will necessitate the consideration of coexistence strategies by service providers. The key decision to be made is whether to retain legacy GPON in the network and combine it with new technologies or to transition completely to XGS-PON and beyond.

articleTitle: Energy Consumption Monitoring and CO2 Emissions Estimation in Optical Access Networks: Abstract
publicationTitle: 2024 International Workshop on Fiber Optics in Access Networks (FOAN)
abstract: The telecommunication infrastructure shows a considerable CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emission footprint, which is growing at an exponential rate due to its expansion resulting from emerging high bandwidth applications. CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> awareness becomes even more important in vertical sectors such as manufacturing, where precise power consumption monitoring is of utmost importance. This paper presents a study of a PON-powered, edge-cloud-based industrial visual inspection use-case as presented by ETSI [1]. We experimentally validate a telemetry framework that provides real-time visibility into the optical network's energy consumption. We use such telemetry to calculate an estimation for the CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emissions associated to our XGS-PON testbed by following the guidelines of the ITU [2].

articleTitle: Node design in Self-Managed Sustainable High-Capacity Optical Networks (SEASON)
publicationTitle: 2024 International Workshop on Fiber Optics in Access Networks (FOAN)
abstract: The goal of the SEASON project [1] is to design and validate a transport network infrastructure able to support beyond 5G and new emerging services, relying on the joint usage of Multi-Band and SDM, spanning the access, aggregation, and metro/long-haul segments, supporting the requirements for x-haul, further integrating the packet/optical and computing layers. The targeted SEASON architecture considers these innovations in addressing sliceable Bandwidth Variable Transceivers (S-BVTs) enabling Point-to-MultiPoint (P2MP) along with the integration of (coherent) pluggable optical modules on open packet/optical white boxes (open devices with hardware and software - referred to as the Network Operating System, - decoupling and providing open control and management interfaces), smart Network Interface Cards (NICs) or the latest generation Data Processing Units (DPU). In this paper, a multi-granular MBoverSDM modular and flexible Optical Switch architecture is presented, that can simplify the node design and enhance switching capabilities in SEASON high capacity packet transport network. Figure 1 displays the node architecture integrated with the RAN, which will be exploited to coordinate user-cell association and latency enforcement in the optical access based on achievable end-to-end latency. Such a node design is capable of dynamically route and add/drop traffic while potentially increasing the switching capacity in a flexible manner. Each layer can include different technology options such as WSSs and/or passive filters for band/spatial multiplexing and demultiplexing, which will offer different levels of flexibility. In the below figure, we depict a 3<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rd</sup> order nodal degree, covering three directions (North, East, and West), in each of which three pairs of optical fibers and three spectral bands (S, C, and L) per fiber are rolled out. This design enables switching at the spectral band level as well as at the wavelength level, facilitated by individual-band WSSs. The node design integrates all essential optical components, including band filters (BF), amplifiers, spatial Optical Cross-Connector (S-OXC) switches, WSSs, and A/D modules. These components are interconnected to establish a modular colorless-directionless (CD) MBoverSDM node architecture, but a colorless-directionless-contentionless (CDC) architecture could be easily implemented by just removing the 1x20 WSS connected to the contentionless NxN WSS or substituting it with additional contentionless MxN WSS.

articleTitle: Next-Generation Long-Reach 100G Passive Optical Networks with Semiconductor Optical Amplifiers
publicationTitle: 2024 International Workshop on Fiber Optics in Access Networks (FOAN)
abstract: This work proposes a future 100G intensity modulation and direct-detection passive optical network with long optical reach using a commercial quantum-well semiconductor optical amplifier.

articleTitle: Satellite-to-ground QKD Feasibility Analysis for High Altitude Rural Areas: A Case Study in Greece
publicationTitle: 2024 International Workshop on Fiber Optics in Access Networks (FOAN)
abstract: This paper is focused on the QKD deployment options for mountain communities based on LEO satellite-to-ground downlinks. The satellite QKD usecase for Vovousa village in Zagori is considered in this paper, providing simulation results for infrastructure deployment options that can support the implementation of LEO satellite DS-BB84 QKD protocol. SKR analysis is provided using an already available key rate calculator, allowing for up to 50kbps key rates with 1.2m receiver apertures in OGS. The use of small sized-OGS as the receiver located in village is also explored, showing ~3kbps SKR.

articleTitle: Implementation and Maintenance Challenges in Home Networking (WiFi7) as the Extension of High-Speed Access Network (xGPON)
publicationTitle: 2024 International Workshop on Fiber Optics in Access Networks (FOAN)
abstract: Founded in 2004, T -2 d.o.o. is celebrating 20 years of innovation in telecommunications. Over the past two decades, we've constantly pushed the boundaries of technology, setting new industry standards. We were the first in Slovenia to introduce VDSL 1 and VDSL2 on copper lines, bring fiber optics directly to users, and pioneer xPON technologies. Our innovations include launching the first video library, 4K television broadcasts, a 7-day time-shift feature, and introducing WiFi 6 and WiFi 6 Mesh technology. With 450 dedicated professionals, we remain committed to delivering top-quality services and leading the future of telecommunications.

articleTitle: Characterization of Photonic Integrated Circuit for Millimeter-Wave-Band Carrier Generation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Workshop on Fiber Optics in Access Networks (FOAN)
abstract: A silicon photonics radio-frequency (RF) synthesizer operating in the millimeter (mm-) wave and sub-THz bands suitable for clock signal distribution in b5G/6G radio access networks is realized and experimentally characterized. The photonic integrated circuit (PIC) operates as a frequency multiplier for an input local oscillator (LO) microwave signal reference, and is specifically designed for maximizing the available optical power level at its output for improved performance of the generated mm-wave band signal. Preliminary measurements performed on two different replicas of the circuit confirms that low-loss dual-tone selection from an on-chip optical frequency comb source can be achieved through high-order multi-resonant photonic integrated filter for the synthesis of 100 GHz and 200 GHz carrier waves.

articleTitle: Investigation of MIMO-DSP for SDM With Weakly-Coupled Multicore Fibers in Access Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Workshop on Fiber Optics in Access Networks (FOAN)
abstract: This paper investigates Multiple Input Multiple Output (MIMO) DSP for space-division multiplexing (SDM) using weakly-coupled multicore fiber (WC-MCF) and intensity modulation-direct detection (IM-DD). A transmission experiment shows limited to no benefit of MIMO DSP in short access networks with 1 km WC-MCF.

articleTitle: Machine Learning for Predicting the Performance of Hybrid Fronthaul Link in 5G/6G Mobile Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Workshop on Fiber Optics in Access Networks (FOAN)
abstract: Due to the commercial deployment of fifth- generation (5G) mobile networks and significant developments in sixth-generation (6G) mobile networks, the existing network framework is undergoing a crunch of bandwidth for fulfilling the bandwidth requirements of end-users. Cloud radio access network (C-RAN) has emerged as a strong contender for handling the enormous data traffic of 5G/6G mobile networks. Although optical fibers are highly recommended for offering the fronthaul connectivity between BBU and RRU in C- RAN architecture, the high installation cost, as well as time- consuming deployment, are the key drawbacks of fiber-based networks. In this work, we are proposing a high-speed fronthaul link comprising a free space optical (FSO) link and a passive optical network (PON) for offering fronthaul connectivity in C-RAN architecture for 5G/6G mobile networks. The proposed link can achieve FSO operating distances of 1.38 km, 0.96 km, and 0.78 km under the effects of light fog (LF), moderate fog (MF), and thick fog (TF) scenarios for SMF of 20 km range and target BER of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-9</sup>. Additionally, we have developed machine learning models for predicting the Q-Factor and signal-to-ratio (SNR) of the proposed link.

articleTitle: Quadrature- Lock Circuit for a Photonic-Delay Phase-Noise Meter
publicationTitle: 2024 International Workshop on Fiber Optics in Access Networks (FOAN)
abstract: Conventional techniques for assessing phase noise depend on a high-performance reference and a phase detector. The delay-line approach eliminates the need for a reference, capitalizing on the low-loss characteristics of optical fiber. However, an accurate calibration of the measuring system remains essential. The quadrature condition on the mixer inputs is vital for proper functionality. This paper introduces a quadrature-lock circuit that features a phase-wrap mechanism. The proposed solution is suitable for use in a cost-effective, photonic-delay, phase-noise measurement setup.

articleTitle: Theory of Mirrorless Lasing and Backward Emission from an Amplifying Layer: Analysis based on Macroscopic Electromagnetism
publicationTitle: 2024 International Workshop on Fiber Optics in Access Networks (FOAN)
abstract: We study the phenomenon of mirrorless lasing and backward emission from the viewpoint of macroscopic electromagnetism by assigning complex permittivity to a light-emitting or amplifying layer. The amplifying medium is described using complex permittivity without detailing the micro-processes in it. The analysis is performed using the well-known Airy formulas for the plane wave normal incidence on a homogeneous dielectric layer. Giant reflection and transmission corresponding to the lasing threshold are obtained by increasing the layer thickness at the fixed value of imaginary part of the layer's permittivity corresponding to gain in it. This result is inherently independent from the incident wave amplitude and denotes the lasing from the both interfaces of the layer (forward and backward emission). At the further increase of the layer's thickness only strong backward emission is observed. The socalled phenomenon of mirrorless lasing is owing to the discontinuation of gain at the boarders of the amplifying layer with surrounding passive media. The backward emission is observed for layers with the gain at the thicknesses longer than that necessary for lasing. The length of the amplifying layer required for the lasing initiation strongly depends on the value of the gain.

articleTitle: Laboratory-Based Investigation of the Performance Efficiencies of a TDM-PON and a WDM-PON
publicationTitle: 2024 International Workshop on Fiber Optics in Access Networks (FOAN)
abstract: In this paper we present a comprehensive, comparative analysis of passive optical networks (PONs) for time-division-multiplexing-and wavelength-division-multiplexing-based passive optical networks (TDM-PONs and WDM-PONs) in terms of their performance efficiency. The PON architecture is now a very effective way to provide high-bandwidth services to end-users. However, the passive optical splitter (POS) leads to a power loss of the optical signal, which limits the overall efficiency of the network. To overcome this limitation, an arrayed waveguide grating (AWG)-based network structure is proposed as an alter-native that enables more efficient optical signal distribution. In the study presented here, experiments were conducted to compare both network architectures. Factors such as the output signal power at the end-user and the quality of the signal reception through the openness of the eye diagram and the bit error rate (BER) were evaluated. The results show that the AWG-based system improves the efficiency of the network through a higher output-signal power, which translates into a better BER.

articleTitle: Rolling-Out High-Speed Networks in Europe: the New Gigabit Infrastructure Act
publicationTitle: 2024 International Workshop on Fiber Optics in Access Networks (FOAN)
abstract: The continuous changes in the digital landscape and the fast and wide adoption of data-intensive applications make it necessary to have proper connections that are reliable and cost-effective. This factor is paramount in order to meet the needs of the industry and the society [1]. In this context, the objectives of the Directive 2014/61/ED, known as the Broadband Cost Reduction Directive, have now become obsolete. This challenge adds up to the fact that the Broadband Cost Reduction Directive was not applied consistently across all EU Member States. It was the view of multiple operators that there was still room for improvement on the progress to be made in relation to multiple elements concerning the ease of access and deployment [2]. With the aim of addressing these aspects while ensuring alignment with the Directive (EU) 2018/1072 establishing the European Electronic Communications Code and for the purposes of facilitating the achievement of the targets laid out in the Digital Decade policy programme, in April 2024 the European Council adopted the Gigabit Infrastructure Act, which replaces the Broadband Cost Reduction Directive.

articleTitle: An Information Distribution System for Realizing High-Speed Communication and Social Infrastructure Management Efficiently
publicationTitle: 2024 International Workshop on Fiber Optics in Access Networks (FOAN)
abstract: This paper proposed new Information Distribution System (IDS) which can provide a high-speed, large-capacity communication service and manage the social infrastructure by using multi-core fiber-based optical network architecture. As a first step for evaluating the effectiveness of proposal, we calculated the crosstalk among cores in multi-core optical fiber using Beam Propagation Method (BPM) on time domain and showed the possibility to estimate the fiber bending direction.

articleTitle: Silicon Photonic Applications to Biomedical Sensors
publicationTitle: 2024 International Workshop on Fiber Optics in Access Networks (FOAN)
abstract: Silicon-based optical probes and biosensors are important tools in biophotonic diagnostic, therapeutic, imaging, and health-status monitoring instrumentation setups. A biosensor is an integrated photonic and electronic device that detects biological or chemical substances (analytes) in a tissue sample. This process can be done through specific optically induced biochemical reactions between the analyte of interest and a layer of biological receptor components such as enzymes, antibodies, nucleic acids, or organelles. Biosensors can detect and evaluate viruses, pathogens, and diseases. Biosensors can be a small optical probe integrated with an electronic device to generate an indicator for communicating, recording, and detecting the changes in the parameters of a biological sample [1]–[3]. Biosensors are applied extensively in point-of-care (POC) testing for medical diagnosis and precise individualized healthcare. POC testing uses mobile devices to analyze tissue samples and body fluids. Major advantages are that POC testing provides on-the-spot results at a hospital bedside or in the clinic, which enables the delivery of accurate results in minutes for clinical decision-making and improve patient care.

articleTitle: Mid-IR FSO Transmission with Directly Modulated QCLs
publicationTitle: 2024 International Workshop on Fiber Optics in Access Networks (FOAN)
abstract: We outline our recent experimental studies on free-space optical (FSO) communications enabled by directly modulated quantum cascade lasers (DM-QCL) operating in the mid-wave infrared (MWIR, 3–5 μm) and long-wave infrared (LWIR, 8–12 μm) regions. Our research compares the performance of unipolar quantum optoelectronic (UQO) devices, including the QCL, and various detector types, such as quantum cascade detectors (QCD) and quantum well-infrared photodetectors (QWIP), each with distinct characteristics. In the last section, we get into the FSO experimental setup and reported results in the atmospheric windows.

articleTitle: Overview of Available Fiber Optic Backhaul Solutions for 5G/6G Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Workshop on Fiber Optics in Access Networks (FOAN)
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive overview of fiber optic backhaul solutions for 5G and 6G networks, emphasizing the critical role of backhaul in supporting ultra-dense, heterogeneous network topologies. The analysis explores the shift of potential bottlenecks to the backhaul segment with the advent of 5G, highlighting the need for high bandwidth, low latency, and reliable connectivity. It compares different fiber optic topologies, evaluates enabling technologies and solutions based on passive optical networks. Special attention is given to TWDM-PON as a flexible and cost-effective solution, capable of meeting the stringent requirements of 5G/6G backhaul.

articleTitle: Clock Synchronization and Network Delay Evaluation Over a Private 5G Standalone Network
publicationTitle: 2024 International Workshop on Fiber Optics in Access Networks (FOAN)
abstract: 5G Standalone (SA) networks are the next generation of cellular networks, with broad applications envisioned in domains including IoT. In this article, we evaluate the feasibility of using Precision Time Protocol (PTP) to tightly synchronize User Equipment (UE) devices connected to a private 5G SA network. Our goal is to achieve submillisecond time synchronization accuracy in order to make the system applicable for industrial-automation IoT networks with stringent timing requirements. We measure the network delay and clock synchronization accuracy through clock comparison utilizing the pulse-per-second output from a UE network card and conclude that the desired accuracy remains challenging, with typical experiments demonstrating multi-millisecond clock offsets with significant and unpredictable drift.
